title: The Smallest Insect Ever Found Is Smaller Than a Single Cell

scenes.text: There's an insect smaller than a single cell.
A fairyfly wasp from Costa Rica. Males can be 0.139 millimetres long, smaller than a one-celled paramecium.
Two human hairs side by side would be wider than this whole animal.
The males are blind and have no wings. They hatch inside the egg of a bark louse, where their mother laid them.
Most never leave that egg. Adults live for hours to a few days, and die where they were born.
Females are bigger: up to half a millimetre. An animal so small it lives and dies inside one egg.

description:
The fairyfly wasp Dicopomorpha echmepterygis is the smallest known insect: males measure 0.139 to 0.24 millimetres, smaller than a single-celled paramecium.
The blind, wingless males develop inside the eggs of a bark louse, most never leave the host egg, and adults live only hours to a few days; females are about 40 percent larger, 0.39 to 0.55 millimetres.
What is the smallest animal you've ever seen with your own eyes?
subject: fairyfly wasp
